title: Security improvement: Azure SSO secrets in env vars instead of a plaintext file?
body:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/65c4486d2e5fdac89759cc06d687838e23f14824/lib/streamlit/config.py#L2753

https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/tutorials/authentication/microsoft

Hello, I would like to be able to pull StreamLit SSO credentials from env vars instead of a plaintext file. It would improve the security of this tool.

comments.body: Another useful feature would be the ability to avoid cred files and env vars entirely, and pull from a key vault. If we could specify this when we import `streamlit` package, perhaps as a constructor, that would improve security too.

This issue requests the ability to configure Azure SSO (and more broadly, `st.login` authentication) secrets via environment variables instead of requiring a plaintext `secrets.toml` file. The author references `lib/streamlit/config.py` and the [Microsoft authentication tutorial](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/tutorials/authentication/microsoft). This is a valid enhancement request for improved secret management flexibility. Notably, Streamlit's `config.toml` already supports environment variable overrides (e.g. `STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT`), but the `[auth]` section of `secrets.toml` does not have an equivalent mechanism. This appears to be a duplicate of #10543, which has significant community interest (78 upvotes).

### Related Issues

- **#10543** — [Set `[auth]` secrets config from environment variables or through `st.login`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10543): This is essentially the same request — allow authentication secrets to be configured via environment variables or `st.login` arguments rather than exclusively through `secrets.toml`. **Likely duplicate.**
- **#7731** — [Allow different paths for storing configuration files](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7731): Related request for more flexible configuration file paths, motivated by deployment environments (e.g. Google Cloud Run) where mounting `secrets.toml` as a volume is problematic.
- **#7946** — [Increase secret management's level of protection](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7946): Broader request to improve the security posture of Streamlit's secret management, including encryption of secrets rather than storing them in plain text.

## Update

Closing this since its possible to set `secrets` programmatically via `st.App`: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14861 see: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/server/st.app

This allows setting secrets from env variables or key vaults.
